answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here. Consider a beacon as the anchor of the cost.
